Speculative decoding is a technique used to make large language models generate text faster. Instead of producing one word at a time, a smaller model first guesses several words ahead. Then the big model checks all those guesses at once and keeps the ones that are correct.

This works because checking text is easier than writing it. The large model can verify a whole chunk in a single step, so fewer passes are needed. If a guess is wrong, the model simply discards it and tries again from that point.

The result is faster output without changing the quality of the text. The final answer still comes from the large model, so accuracy stays the same. Speculative decoding is now common in many AI systems because it saves time and computing power.
